body:
Adds `command-stream/core` so shell-only consumers can use `$`, ProcessRunner and virtual commands without loading compatibility layers, terminals or development tools. Core loads 70 ESM / 71 CommonJS modules, compared with 284 for the full entry.

Fixes #235

## Changes

- Share the existing shell implementation, built-in commands, registrations, settings and runner identity between the full entry, typed ESM/CommonJS core entries and `process-runner`.
- Separate virtual-command composition and metadata from the package installer that imports Execa.
- Enforce fewer than 100 cold-loaded non-builtin modules in both core formats. Reject compatibility, terminal, REPL/debugger and testing modules in the graph; bundle and execute core without those inputs.
- Document the public core API and prepare its minor release with a changeset.
- Update Execa to 10.2.1 after [its strict TypeScript blocker](https://github.com/sindresorhus/execa/issues/1265) closed. Update fancy-regex and both Rust lockfiles to fix dependency freshness checks, with a Rust patch fragment.
- Retry Deno imports only when esm.sh reports HTTP 408 while a cold build is queued: at most three attempts, with 5- and 10-second delays. Preserve live stderr and a bounded diagnostic tail; persistent timeouts, compiler errors and runtime failures remain fatal. Both real HTTP probes remain required.

The issue explicitly allows the lightweight-subpath approach. The full API remains available; installed dependency size is unchanged. The `parity-exempt` label applies to JavaScript's module-loader graph, which has no Rust counterpart. Executable language parity checks remain enabled.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

Run `node experiments/issue-235/import-probe.mjs command-stream` or substitute `command-stream/core`. Before implementation, the full entry loaded 284 modules in approximately 461 ms on Linux / Node 26.12.1. Commit `7bb8fe2` preserves four failing core regressions before the subpath existed. Module count is the deterministic CI budget; elapsed time is diagnostic.

`core-entry.test.mjs` checks fresh ESM/CommonJS loads, the module budget, executable bundling, real commands, synchronous and exact-argv execution, virtual pipelines, shared state and API identity. Strict TypeScript consumers verify both declaration formats.

The [previous Deno failure](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40077631780/job/120825515833) belongs to `285f44b`, created 2026-10-24T08:20:11Z. Downloaded job-log line 550 reports an esm.sh Execa import returning HTTP 408; line 565 records exit code 1. The same dependency import and immutable GitHub-head URL failed locally, and the CDN status endpoint confirmed queued builds. The queue subsequently recovered and both real probes passed locally. Ten mocked regression tests verify retry success, exhaustion, ANSI diagnostics and immediate failure for other errors. No manual action is required.

## Validation

- Full Bun suite: **2,812 passed, 10 skipped, zero failures** across 179 files, including all ten CDN retry regressions.
- Node core budget, bundling, execution and shared-state checks: **5 passed**.
- Both real Deno CDN probes passed locally, exercising the HTTP-served checkout and immutable GitHub head, shell execution, ShellJS identity, normal brace globs and depth protection.
- Lint, formatting, duplication and strict TypeScript checks passed. The pre-commit hook also passed.
- Existing Node regression suite: **124 passed**; zx: **490 passed, 2 skipped**; Execa: **38 passed**.
- Rust all-feature suite including doctests: **905 passed, 7 ignored**. Formatting, Clippy and rustdoc with warnings denied, and generated documentation checks passed.
- Declared and installed dependency freshness checks passed. Package dry-run includes the core source files and both declaration formats.

CI on `4f88be8eb7d7fa93cd84410cbc1c2933de003f2c`: **49 passed, zero failed or pending**, with six release-only jobs correctly skipped on this PR. All eight workflows completed successfully:

- [JavaScript checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451213), including the [Deno CDN check](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451213/job/120830175205), all Node/Bun platform suites and production-install modes.
- [Rust checks and package validation](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451166), including Linux, macOS and Windows.
- [Dependency freshness](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451195), [repository quality](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451186), [language parity](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451135), [workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451176), [benchmarks](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451143) and [security](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451146).

Downloaded Deno job-log lines 605–608 and 625–628 confirm both real probes executed all assertions successfully. The first Windows Rust attempt stalled in the existing PID-identity test and was cancelled for log collection; the [targeted rerun](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/40079451166/job/120832921106) passed on the same commit, including that test and all doctests. Both attempts' logs are preserved locally. No checks were disabled or relaxed.

The latest default branch is included, the working tree is clean, and the complete diff has been reviewed. Implementation and verification are complete; this PR is ready for review and remains unmerged.

body:
Caught virtual `exit 7` failures previously populated stderr with `Command failed with exit code 7` and mirrored that text to the parent process. Under `set('e')`, even `exit 0` rejected. This change makes both statuses silent and lets successful exits resolve.

Fixes #213.

## Changes

- Throw only for nonzero statuses, with explicit empty stderr. The runner retains the existing status aliases and decides whether to reject according to errexit.
- Remove the exit handler's dependency on global shell settings.
- Preserve sequence stopping after a failing exit under errexit, including when capture is disabled; unexpected virtual-handler failures still report their diagnostic stderr.
- Add eight regression tests to the existing Bun suite and Node 22/24/26 CI jobs.
- Add a reusable reproduction and a patch changeset for the next npm release.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

```sh
node experiments/issue-213/virtual-exit.mjs 2>stderr.txt
bun experiments/issue-213/virtual-exit.mjs 2>stderr.txt
node --test js/tests/virtual-exit.test.mjs
bun test js/tests/virtual-exit.test.mjs --timeout 10000
```

Before implementation, six of eight tests failed under both runtimes. The nine-case probe showed bogus stderr for caught nonzero exits and rejected status 0 under errexit. After the fix, all observations have empty stderr and `stderr.txt` is empty. `exit 7` rejects under errexit, while `exit 0` and argumentless `exit` resolve. A real child process provides the silent-status comparison.

Tests also verify result/error status aliases, output and exit events, stopping a sequence after `exit 3`, default mirroring, disabled mirroring/capture, non-errexit results, and unexpected-handler diagnostics.

## Validation

- Focused Bun suite: 61 passed; Node exit regression suite: 8 passed.
- Existing Node regression suites plus the new exit tests: 104 passed.
- `bun run check`: ESLint, repository formatting, duplication, and TypeScript declarations passed.
- Documentation/workflow regression checks: 386 passed.
- All 29 executable features agree under Node and Bun and run in Rust.
- Full Bun suite: 2,574 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed across 153 files.
- Full Rust suite, including doc tests: 830 passed, 5 ignored, 0 failed.
- Node zx compatibility: 490 passed, 2 skipped; Execa compatibility: 38 passed.
- Generated documentation and changeset/version validation passed.
- All seven CI workflows pass on `f9f55a0`, including Bun on Linux/macOS/Windows, Node 22/24/26, process-tree checks, security, quality, dependency freshness, executable parity, and benchmark smoke checks: [JavaScript checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/37572496651).

The first macOS Node 24 process-tree job observed one extra heartbeat byte (`6 !== 5`) in the existing `exec: stubborn` test at `js/tests/windows-tree-kill.test.mjs:87` (preserved run log, line 1806). Its 19 tests passed on a single rerun of the same commit: [successful rerun](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/37572496651/job/112635408432). The initial failure and rerun logs are preserved in `ci-logs/`. The new exit regressions passed in every runtime job on the first attempt.

## Scope and release

This is JavaScript-specific and carries `parity-exempt`: Rust's exit handler already returns the requested code with empty stderr. Executable language parity remains enabled. Existing argument parsing and non-errexit sequence behavior are preserved; full POSIX shell termination semantics are outside this issue's fix.

`js/.changeset/issue-213-virtual-exit.md` prepares the next patch release. Package versions remain managed by the release workflow.

<!-- hive-mind:changes:start -->
### Changes
- 7 file(s) modified
- 233 line(s) added
- 3 line(s) removed
- Files:
  - `.github/workflows/js.yml`
  - `experiments/issue-213/README.md`
  - `experiments/issue-213/virtual-exit.mjs`
  - `js/.changeset/issue-213-virtual-exit.md`
  - `js/src/$.mjs`
  - `js/src/commands/$.exit.mjs`
  - `js/tests/virtual-exit.test.mjs`
<!-- hive-mind:changes:end -->

body:
Closes #14.

## What the issue asked

> How `tee` command is implemented? Is it possible to reproduce it in pure js?
> May be we should have such a virtual command [...] Does `tee` command support interactive mode?

Yes to the first — and it already existed. The second answer is "no, and here is
why", documented in both READMEs rather than papered over.

## Root cause

`js/src/commands/$.tee.mjs` was present in the tree but **never registered**.
`registerBuiltins()` in `js/src/$.mjs` skipped it, so every `` $`tee ...` ``
fell through to `/bin/sh -l -c 'tee ...'` and ran the system GNU binary. The
existing tee tests passed because they were exercising `/usr/bin/tee`, not this
code.

Reproduced before fixing:

```console
$ node -e "import('./js/src/\$.mjs').then(({listCommands}) => console.log(listCommands().includes('tee')))"
false
```

Now `` $`which tee` `` reports `tee: shell builtin`, which the test suite
asserts so the command cannot silently fall back to the system binary again.

## A second bug found on the way

Running the new example under Node returned `"INHERIT"` instead of the piped
text. That is not a tee bug — it reproduces on a clean `main`:

```console
$ node -e "import('./js/src/\$.mjs').then(async ({\$}) => console.log((await \$\`echo hello | cat\`).stdout))"
inherit
```

The `stdin` option carries **either** input data **or** one of the stdio mode
keywords (`inherit`, `ignore`, `pipe`). Both virtual command runners treated any
string as data, so the mode keyword became the command's input. `runVirtualHandler`
compounded it by spreading `...options` *after* `stdin: currentInput`, letting the
pipeline's own stdin option overwrite input piped from the previous stage.

Fixed with a single `stdinDataFromOptions()` helper in `js/src/$.stream-utils.mjs`
used by both runners, and by moving the options spread ahead of `args`/`stdin`.

Rust is unaffected by construction: `StdinOption` keeps modes and content in
separate variants, so a mode can never be read as data. Tests lock that in.

## Cross-language parity

Per review feedback, `tee` is implemented in **both** supported languages, not
just JavaScript:

| | JavaScript | Rust |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Implementation | `js/src/commands/$.tee.mjs` | `rust/src/commands/tee.rs` |
| Registration | `registerBuiltins()` in `js/src/$.mjs` | `try_virtual_command` in `lib.rs` and `pipeline.rs` |
| Listed by `which` | ✅ | ✅ (`rust/src/commands/which.rs`) |
| Tests | 18 in `js/tests/builtin-commands.test.mjs` | 10 unit + 14 integration |

Both follow GNU coreutils 9.4: `-a`/`--append`, `-i`/`--ignore-interrupts`,
clustered short flags (`-ai`), `--` as an option terminator, a bare `-` treated
as a file named `-`, input always copied to stdout, and a write failure reported
on stderr with exit code 1 while the remaining files are still written.

## Reproduction and verification

| Behaviour | Test |
| --- | --- |
| `tee` resolves to the built-in, not the system binary | `tee should be a virtual command, not the system binary` |
| Mode keyword is never command input | `virtual-command-stdin.test.mjs`, `node-process-regressions.mjs`, `test_stdin_mode_is_not_virtual_command_input` |
| Piped input beats the `stdin` option | `piped input wins over the pipeline stdin option` (bun + node + Rust) |
| Write failure continues, exact stderr | `builtin-commands.test.mjs`, `builtin_commands.rs` |
| Each README example | `tee should keep a mid-pipeline stage flowing`, `test_readme_tee_pipeline_example` |

The three Node regression tests fail on a clean `main` and pass here, which is
what makes this a verified fix rather than an assumed one.

## On interactive mode

Virtual commands receive stdin as **one completed buffer**: a pipeline reads each
upstream stage to the end before handing the result on. So this `tee` is a
pipeline stage, not a live terminal filter, and cannot echo keystrokes as you
type them. The `interactive: true` option applies to spawned system processes.
This is stated in both READMEs and in `js/examples/tee-command.mjs` instead of
being claimed as supported.

## A third bug found on the way (CI)

The first push of these tests passed on Linux and timed out on Windows and
macOS. Root cause, reproduced locally rather than guessed:

`bun test` evaluates `js/tests/test-helper.mjs` **once**, so the
`beforeEach`/`afterEach` reset hooks it registers at module scope belong to
whichever test file imported it first. Every later file runs with no cleanup, so
a file such as `js/tests/raw-function.test.mjs` — which calls
`disableVirtualCommands()` in its own `beforeEach` — leaves virtual commands
disabled for the files that follow it. Bun's file order is neither alphabetical
nor identical across platforms, which is why only two runners failed.

With virtual commands disabled, `` $`cat` `` is the real binary, and a real
command run with `stdin: 'inherit'` never finishes: the runner pumps the parent's
stdin into a pipe and the child waits for an EOF that never arrives. Hence the
10 s timeout and exit code 143.

`experiments/issue-14/stdin-inherit-blocks.mjs` reproduces that hang in one
command under both runtimes. The tests now enable virtual commands themselves
and assert the stdin invariant through a purpose-built probe command that spawns
nothing, so they no longer depend on state left by unrelated files.

Note for a follow-up, out of scope here: that `stdin: 'inherit'` hang is
pre-existing behaviour on `main` under both Bun and Node, and it happens even
when the parent's stdin is `/dev/null`. This PR does not change it.

## Also in this PR

- `js/examples/tee-command.mjs` replaces three ad-hoc example scripts
  (`test-unix-tee.mjs`, `test-virtual-tee.mjs`, `tee-interactive-demo.mjs`).
- `js/README.md` claimed 18 built-in commands while already enumerating 21; the
  real count with `tee` is 22.
- One changeset in `js/.changeset/` and a fragment in `rust/changelog.d/` so the
  release automation picks this up.

## Local checks

`bun run lint`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run check:duplication`,
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`,
`cargo test --all-features` (470 passed), `node --test` Node suites (9 passed),
and `BASE_REF=main .github/scripts/check-language-parity.sh` all pass.

`bun test js/tests/` reports 1440 pass / 11 skip / 28 fail; all 28 are `jq`
tests that fail identically on a clean `main` because `jq` is not installed in
this sandbox. CI installs it. The full suite was also run with stdin held open
(`sleep 600 | bun test js/tests/`) to prove no test blocks on inherited stdin:
no timeouts.
title: feat(commands): add tee as a virtual command in JavaScript and Rust

This adds the command builders, terminal buffer, command package ecosystem, stream processing, and development tools requested by all six child issues of #224. Existing ESM, CommonJS, lightweight ProcessRunner, zx, ShellJS, and Execa entry points remain covered by their compatibility suites.

| Issue | Delivered behavior |
| --- | --- |
| #1 | `$fy`, `command-stream fy`, and `fy(source)` produce executable ES modules that preserve shell arguments, stdin, heredocs, control flow, and status. Rust provides the translator and CLI too. |
| #9 | Independent writable terminal buffers, changed-frame subscriptions, resizing, and plain/colored text snapshots using the existing xterm/headless and vt100 emulators. |
| #30 | Typed command packages; atomic install/reload/uninstall; composition, inheritance, middleware, wrapped generators, npm installation/search; ten installable example packages plus Git, deployment, ls-color, and enterprise workflows. |
| #31 | Pull-driven map/filter/reduce/forEach, UTF-8 lines, bounded split/merge, windows/batches, live error-rate/latency/throughput statistics, monitoring/alerts, and measured buffered comparison. Native and generator pumps now respect stream capacity. |
| #32 | Watch/restart and package reload; JavaScript/shell REPL and completion; browser pipeline debugger with stepping, data previews, flow, profiling, memory and timeline; packageable VS Code extension; command mocks, pipeline assertions and output snapshots. |
| #34 | Immutable lazy exact-argv builders with option transforms, run/await/stream, exit-code selection and POSIX string rendering, with a Rust builder counterpart. |

The [complete requirement inventory, alternatives, primary-source research, and acceptance plan](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-224-7434d5c60324/dev/log/issues/224/pulls/225/analysis/requirements.md) covers every issue and comment. None of the six issues was already completely resolved. Portable core APIs have Node/Bun/Rust feature examples; JavaScript module packages, the JavaScript evaluator and IDE/browser tools are documented as JavaScript integrations.

Reproduction and regression coverage:

- The focused acceptance tests failed before implementing the missing APIs. See `js/tests/advanced-command.test.mjs`, `advanced-stream.test.mjs`, `command-packages.test.mjs`, `development-tools.test.mjs`, `terminal-buffer.test.mjs`, and the matching Rust integration tests.
- `experiments/issue-224/pipeline-pressure.mjs` reproduces eager production through the old native pipeline: all 200 chunks were produced while downstream was paused. The integration test now verifies bounded production and preservation of all 3,276,800 bytes in Node and Bun.
- `advanced-integration.test.mjs` verifies slow consumers retain output after child exit, cancellation interrupts an idle merged command, inherited stdin forwards EOF and stops waiting after child exit, invalid package reloads preserve working handlers, watcher shutdown/restarts, REPL behavior, debugger controls, extension providers, and all ten package examples.
- Finite Node/Bun cancellation probes reproduce a native stage surviving mixed-pipeline cancellation; shared process-tree termination and forceful escalation now stop it. A worker capped at 16 MiB reproduces the editor regex stall; disjoint escape alternatives complete the same input.
- A symlinked watch root reproduces macOS retaining old package handlers. Watch snapshots and package entry paths now use canonical identities; the regressions and independent Node/Bun probes verify reload through linked directories, including Node with `--preserve-symlinks`.
- Preloading a disabled virtual registry reproduces the CI REPL/mock failures. All five new suites now use the existing cleanup hooks, and watched fixtures save atomically. The full Bun suite and the preload regression both pass. [CI findings and exact log locations](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-224-7434d5c60324/dev/log/issues/224/pulls/225/analysis/ci-investigation.md) are preserved.
- The finite memory probe processes 100,000 records (25.6 MB) in separate Node processes with a 128 MiB heap limit. Observed RSS growth was 13,369,344 bytes for streaming and 84,529,152 for buffering. These are single-run measurements, not a universal performance guarantee; [methodology and results](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-224-7434d5c60324/dev/log/issues/224/pulls/225/analysis/measurements.md) are preserved.

Local validation passed:

- Full Bun suite: 2,688 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed.
- Rust `cargo test --all-features`: 838 passed, 5 ignored, 0 failed; formatting, Clippy across all targets/features with warnings denied, and rustdoc checks passed. Builds used one job and reduced debug data within the container memory budget.
- Node runner/terminal/CJS regressions: 104 passed. Node zx/Execa compatibility and production artifact tests: 524 passed, 2 skipped.
- ESLint, repository Prettier, strict ESM/CJS declarations, duplication gate (2.57%), frozen lockfile installation, npm packaging, and VSIX packaging passed.
- All 34 Node/Bun/Rust executable feature examples passed parity; generated documentation is current. All 211 tracked-documentation checks passed.
- Browser verification exercised Pause/Step/Resume and error inspection; the browser was closed afterward. The new debugger has no previous UI to compare against.

![Pipeline debugger showing stream flow, inspected data and profiling](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-224-7434d5c60324/docs/screenshots/pipeline-debugger.png?raw=true)

Final verification on `417df1d`: all eight GitHub workflows pass, including [JavaScript](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/38123983855), [Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/38123983889), and [Security/CodeQL](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/actions/runs/38123983896). The separate CodeQL findings check passes, and both earlier alerts are fixed. The matrices cover Node 22/24/26, Bun on Linux/macOS/Windows, and Rust on Linux/macOS/Windows. Conditional release jobs skip for pull requests.

- [x] Reviewed the final diff and all comment types; verified fresh CI timestamps and the exact head SHA; preserved and fixed the failing-log findings.
- [x] Verified the latest main is included, the working tree is clean, the complete scope and documentation agree, and PR 225 is ready for review.

Behavior and release notes: translation delegates shell semantics to the original interpreter and requires that shell plus command-stream; it is not an AST-to-JavaScript compiler. Existing result-returning virtual handlers and explicit capture/composition retain complete input/output strings; use native stages, generators and `capture:false` for bounded processing. Package entry reload preserves relative imports while imported dependencies retain their runtime cache; a process restart reloads the whole graph. Ten example packages and the extension are ready for independent publication; published-package counts, extension downloads, adoption and user feedback are post-release success metrics and are not claimed as achieved. A JavaScript minor changeset and Rust minor release fragment prepare the library releases without manually changing release-managed versions.

body:
## Summary

This PR resolves all seven open issues (#226–#232) as #233 asks. Each requirement is mapped to its implementation and to a test that reproduces the problem without the change in [`dev/log/issues/233/pulls/234/analysis/requirements.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-233-b89721e32913/dev/log/issues/233/pulls/234/analysis/requirements.md).

### #226: crates.io trusted publishing
- The `release` and `instant-release` jobs in `.github/workflows/rust.yml` get `id-token: write`.
- They run `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action` (pinned to v1.0.5) with `continue-on-error: true`.
- They publish with `steps.crates_auth.outputs.token || secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN || secrets.CARGO_TOKEN`. This follows the issue's policy comment: OIDC first, token secrets kept as the fallback.
- `.github/scripts/publish-preflight.mjs` checks the OIDC token first (`js/tests/publish-preflight.test.mjs`).
- The setup is documented in `.github/DEPLOYMENT.md`.

### #227: `$({ timeout })`
- The JS `timeout` option (ms) covers simple commands, pipelines, `stream()`, exec specs and `.sync()`.
- It combines with a caller `signal`, reports `result.timedOut`, and rejects invalid values with a `TypeError`.
- Rust parity: `RunOptions::timeout`, `StreamingRunner::timeout` and `timed_out()`.
- Tests: `js/tests/timeout-option.test.mjs`, `rust/tests/timeout.rs`.

### #228: non-login shell by default
- Command strings now run with `sh -c` instead of `-l -c`, so profile files no longer print into captured output or override the `PATH` from `env`.
- `loginShell: true` restores the old behaviour.
- `js/tests/login-shell.test.mjs` uses the issue's `HOME`/`.profile` reproduction.

### #229: removing environment variables
- Rust:
  - `RunOptions::env_remove`
  - `StreamingRunner::env_remove`/`env_remove_all`
  - `TerminalCaptureOptions::env_remove`/`env_clear`, forwarded to `portable_pty::CommandBuilder`
- JS: an `env` value of `undefined` removes that variable from the child.
- Tests: `rust/tests/env_remove.rs`, `rust/tests/terminal_options.rs` (the issue's `SECRET_TOKEN` case), `js/tests/env-undefined-removes.test.mjs`.

### #230: live stdin with an exact argv (Rust)
- `StreamingRunner::stdin_pipe()` keeps stdin open. `OutputStream::write_stdin`/`close_stdin` work while output streams.
- `ProcessRunner::from_argv(program, args, options)` skips the shell and virtual commands.
- Tests: `rust/tests/stdin_pipe.rs`, `rust/tests/process_argv.rs`.

### #231: terminal artifact selection
- JS `artifacts: [...]` and Rust `TerminalCaptureOptions::artifacts` select the files to write. Renderers for unselected files are skipped, so no GIF is rendered unless one is asked for.
- Rust also gets:
  - `recording.gif`, encoded with `gif` and drawn with `font8x8` glyphs, so no SVG rasteriser is needed;
  - `aspect_ratio`;
  - `on_trace`.
- Tests: `js/tests/terminal-artifact-selection.test.mjs`, `rust/tests/terminal_options.rs`.

### #232: fire-and-forget detached spawn
- JS `spawnDetached()`, `runner.spawnDetached()` and `$({ detached: true })`:
  - start the command in its own session with ignored stdio and `unref()`;
  - resolve with `{ pid }` on `spawn` and reject on `error`.
- Rust `StreamingRunner::detach()` and `ProcessRunner::spawn_detached()` do the same.
- Tests: `js/tests/detached-spawn.test.mjs` (pid = pgid, session leader, outlives the caller), `rust/tests/detach.rs`.

Docs, feature-catalog examples (JS Node/Bun and Rust, checked by `scripts/check-parity.mjs`), a changeset and a Rust changelog fragment are included.

## CI fixes needed along the way

| Check | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JS tests on Bun 1.4.4 | Bun 1.4.4 replaced the glob matcher that `js/src/bun-shell/glob.mjs` ports, and nesting is no longer limited to 10 levels | The test checks the ported v1.4.2 limit directly (probe: `experiments/issue-233/bun-glob-nesting.mjs`) |
| JS tests on macOS | macOS `ps` has no `sid` keyword | The session leader is read from the `s` in `ps -o stat` |
| Benchmarks `--locked` | `gif`/`font8x8` were missing from `rust/benchmarks/Cargo.lock` | Lockfile updated |
| Language parity | Bumping tokio in `rust/benchmarks/Cargo.toml` counted as a Rust benchmark change, but JS benchmark dependencies live in `js/package.json`, which is never counted | `.github/scripts/check-language-parity.sh` treats the benchmark manifest like its lockfile. A new benchmark target still adds a source file and is caught (`js/tests/language-parity.test.mjs`) |
| Dependency freshness (also red on `main`) | Newer releases of eslint, eslint-plugin-prettier, jscpd, tokio, libc, vt100, ureq and execa | All updated except execa. vt100 0.18 takes `NonZeroU16` sizes and returns `String` state, and terminal capture converts at that boundary. vt100 is not part of the public API |

### execa is held at 10.1.1
execa 10.2.0's own declarations fail to type-check with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `skipLibCheck: false`:

```
TS2344 in types/return/result-all.d.ts: Types of property 'preferLocal' are incompatible.
```

command-stream re-exports those types and checks them with these settings.

- I reported it upstream: https://github.com/sindresorhus/execa/issues/1265. The minimal reproduction is in `experiments/issue-233/execa-types/`.
- Because JSON has no comments, the freshness check now reads npm blockers from `js/dependency-blockers.json`. The blocker counts only while its issue is open.
- The bare `npm outdated` step became `bun scripts/check-dependencies.mjs --installed-npm`. That step still fails when a lockfile falls behind its declaration (tests in `js/tests/dependency-freshness.test.mjs`).

## Maintainer step after merge (#226)
Register the trusted publisher on crates.io:

```
package-registry-manager setup --registry crates-io --migrate --execute
```

Until then, releases keep publishing through the token fallback.
